# Balor: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Balor** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Balor Son of Dot, Grandson of Nét.** The book of invasions fixes Balor's place before it tells his deeds: Balor mac Doit meic Néit, 'Balor son of Dot, grandson of Nét', king of the Fomorians — the sea-going race who had pressed on Ireland since the age of the Nemedians, exacting tribute from the outer islands.  His wife was Cethlenn of the crooked teeth, and it was her spear, or the wound she dealt at Mag Tuired, that killed the Dagda at the Brug years later — the Lebor Gabála records the All-Father's death from Cethlenn's blow as the long-settled price of Balor's war. His daughter was Ethniu, and she was given to Cian, son of Dian Cécht the healer; their son was Lugh, the Samildánach, equally skilled in all arts.

**How the Eye Was Poisoned.** Cath Maige Tuired explains the weapon before it uses it.  Balor had a destructive eye, never opened except on a battlefield, and four men were needed to raise its lid with a polished handle that passed through it.  Any army that eye looked upon was made worthless, though it were many thousands strong.

**The Tower and the Prophecy.** The medieval manuscripts know that Ethniu was Balor's daughter and Lugh's mother; how that came to be is told by the oral tradition of the north-west, collected in the nineteenth century on and around Tory Island — Balor's sea-girt fortress off the Donegal coast.  A druid foretold that Balor would die by the hand of his own grandson, and the king answered the prophecy with masonry: he locked his daughter Eithne in a tower on the rock, with twelve matrons to keep every man from her sight. The doom came in by the usual door.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Balor
- **ASCII form:** balor
- **Meaning:** "Fomorian king whose destructive eye blasts armies when its lid is raised, slain by his grandson Lúg with a sling-stone at Cath Maige Tuired."
- **Domain of influence:** Destruction, Evil Eye, Fomorians
- **Pantheon:** Celtic
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 65 of 449

## The Name Travels

Balor's clearest cross-border witnesses are comparative, not cognate.  The Welsh corpus preserves no figure derived from the same name — the Brythonic silence is total, as it is for so many of the Fomorian cycle.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Balor** stands at [/balor/](/balor/) — [lore](/balor/lore/), [scholars](/balor/scholars/), [patterns](/balor/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. The restoration keeps one feature the ASCII form drops. One is enough to matter, and the label says so plainly: Tier-2.
